expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: Five interfaces (Trialing, Active, Canceling, PastDue, Canceled) each with `readonly status: "trialing"|"active"|"canceling"|"past_due"|"canceled"`; combined as `SubscriptionState = Trialing | Active | Canceling | PastDue | Canceled`

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Canceled has {status, canceledAt, accessEndsAt, cancellation}; Trialing has {status, trialEndsAt, convertsToPriceId}; no overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: `function assertNever(x: never)` defined; used in `entitlement()` switch with five cases covering all states plus default; recommends `@typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check`

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PriceId all `Brand<string, ...>`; RetryCount as `Brand<number, ...>` with range validation

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Single `transition(sub: Subscription, event: SubscriptionEvent, clock: Clock): Result<Subscription, TransitionError>` function; all fields readonly; 'The only ways to obtain a Subscription are parseSubscription and transition'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists 6 numbered misuses in 'First, the misuse enumeration' section; e.g., '`voluntary: boolean` + `cancelReason: string` are independently settable...permits `voluntary: true, reason: "payment_failed"`' — then explains nested union prevents this

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union; lists as first misuse: '6 optional fields claim 2^6 = 64 states. You have 4.'
